findings.evidence: Container: toast; Placement: in a dialog centered on the password reset step, over the new password field it blocks
findings.fix: Present this message in a persistent modal or inline block that stays until the reader acts, not a self-clearing toast.
findings.violation: The expired-link failure fully blocks the reader from setting a new password at all, yet it is presented in a self-clearing toast, so a reader who looks away misses the one message explaining why the step cannot proceed.

findings.evidence: This field takes a maximum of 30 characters. Shorten the entry and save again.
findings.fix: Add a brief reason for the limit, e.g. "This field takes a maximum of 30 characters so it fits on a shipping label. Shorten the entry and save again."
findings.violation: The message states a product-set limit (a 30-character maximum) with no reason attached, leaving the reader to simply comply without understanding why the limit exists.

findings.evidence: The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered. Contact support for assistance.
findings.fix: Add a brief acknowledgment before the technical facts, e.g. "We're sorry, your last changes weren't saved and can't be recovered. Contact support for help restoring them."
findings.violation: This is the only message block on this screen, its Suggested fix is none, and it reports a completed, unrecoverable loss, yet the wording is a bare technical notice with no acknowledgment of what that loss means for the reader.

findings.evidence: Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502.
findings.fix: Replace the code or jargon term with a plain-language sentence a non-technical reader can act on.
findings.violation: The message text carries an internal error code, a code-style token, or an engineering-jargon term standing in for a plain-language explanation.

findings.evidence: Receipts upload as PDF or PNG only, the two formats the expense system can read.
findings.fix: Validate the file's format immediately after selection and show this message at that point instead of waiting for submit.
findings.violation: This message fires on-submit for a predictable mistake, but the file's format is already known the moment it is selected, so the product could have warned the reader before they submitted rather than waiting until then.

findings.evidence: Placement: at the top of a long form, requiring the reader to scroll up to see it, though the field itself stays visible on the page
findings.fix: Move the message to directly beside or below the password field instead of the top of the form.
findings.violation: The message sits at the top of a long form rather than beside the password field it concerns, requiring the reader to scroll up to find it even though the field itself stays visible.
